headlines.article_text: Stocks moving the most today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this photo illustration, a smartphone displays the logo of Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (NYSE: HPE), an American multinational information technology company specializing in enterprise networking, cloud services, data storage and computing solutions, in front of a screen showing the company's latest stock market chart on February 26, 2026 in Qianjiang, Hubei Province, China. Cheng Xin | Getty Images In extended trading, shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise slumped despite the company offering an outlook that surpassed the Street's estimates. Agilent Technologies rose after the bell, catching a tailwind from its stronger-than-anticipated forecast for the current quarter. Follow below as CNBC highlights the biggest stock moves of the day. 15 Min Ago SharkNinja set to join the S&P 500; shares rise in extended trading The manufacturer of the Ninja Creami ice cream maker will join the S&P 500 index on Dec. 2. SharkNinja will be replacing Virginia-based utility AES Corp, which is being taken private by a consortium of investors that includes BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners in a $33.4 billion deal. SharkNinja on Monday In turn, Paycom Software will move up to the S&P MidCap 400, taking SharkNinja's place in that index. Shares of SharkNinja were last up 2% in extended trading. — Darla Mercado 52 Min Ago Zoom shares are flat despite earnings beat and higher outlook Shares of Zoom Communications were up nearly 6% during the day, but were near the flat line in extended trading after the company reported its third quarter earnings of fiscal year 2027. Zoom -YTD Adjusted earnings were $1.59 per share, above analysts' $1.49 estimate, according to LSEG. Revenue was $1.29 billion, surpassing the consensus estimate of $1.28 billion. Enterprise revenue of $805.4 million topped the FactSet consensus estimate $795.6 million. Free cash flow of $558.1 million beat the $477.6 million consensus estimate. Zoom forecast fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.55 to $1.57 per share and revenue of $1.293 billion to $1.298 billion. It raised its full-year earnings outlook and declared its first quarterly dividend of 25 cents per share. — Deena Zaidi 1 Hour Ago HPE falls after hours despite stronger-than-expected outlook, earnings beat Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares fell about 5% in extended trading after gaining nearly 13% during the regular session, as AI stocks rallied broadly. HPE- YTD The company reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $14.55 billion, slightly above the LSEG consensus estimate of $14.50 billion. Free cash flow of $1.92 billion, topping the $1.24 billion estimate, per FactSet. For the current quarter, the company's forecast adjusted earnings of $1.30 to $1.40 per share, above the FactSet consensus estimate of $1.07, and revenue of $14 billion to $14.6 billion, versus $12.99 billion. For fiscal 2027, HPE projected adjusted earnings of $5.05 to $5.35 per share and revenue of $59.4 billion to $63.1 billion. That's above FactSet consensus estimates of $4.76 per share and $55.10 billion, respectively. Hewlett Packard also authorized an additional $5 billion in share repurchases and raised its quarterly dividend 22.8%, to 17.5 cents per share. — Deena Zaidi 1 Hour Ago Semtech shares drop despite the company beating estimates Shares of Semtech were down 8.5% despite the semiconductors provider beating analyst consensus on earnings per share and revenue. SMTC on Monday Semtech reported $1.17 in earnings per share, excluding items, and $423 million in revenue for the third quarter. Analysts polled by FactSet expected $1.13 earnings per share and $416.7 million in revenue. For the fourth quarter, the company expects earnings per share of $1.30 to $1.36, excluding items, and revenue of $475 million to $485 million. Both are above FactSet consensus estimates of $1.29 per share and $449.3 million. — Ananya Chetia 1 Hour Ago Symbiotic slumps after revenue forecast largely disappoints The automation technology company slipped in extended trading. Guidance for first quarter revenue ranges from $805 million to $825 million, while the FactSet consensus sought $822 million. Symbiotic shares were last off almost 4%. Symbiotic on Monday In the fourth quarter, adjusted EBITDA of $113.9 million and revenue of $777.6 million beat analysts' respective estimates of $103.9 million and $774.2 million, per LSEG. — Darla Mercado 1 Hour Ago Peloton Interactive jumps on $300 million share buyback announcement The fitness tech company saw shares pop 3% in extended trading after announcing that its board has authorized a $300 million share repurchase program. Peloton on Monday This program doesn't obligate Peloton to buy a specific amount of shares. — Darla Mercado 2 Hours Ago Agilent Technologies rises in after-hours trading after guidance surpasses estimates Shares of Agilent Technologies jumped 7% after the company shared an outlook that topped the Street's expectations. Current-quarter guidance calls for adjusted earnings of $1.54 to $1.57 per share on revenue of $8 billion to $8.15 billion. The FactSet consensus estimate was $1.50 per share and $1.92 billion. Agilent's full-year forecast also came in ahead of analysts' expectations. — Darla Mercado 5 Hours Ago Mining stocks rally alongside the price of gold and copper December gold futures rallied Monday Mining stocks rallied Monday alongside bullish moves in the price of gold, silver and copper. Gold futures climbed about 4%, silver by roughly 5% and copper added nearly 3%. Newmont Mining , AngloGold Ashanti , Coeur Mining and Gold Fields Ltd. all surged more than 7%, while Freeport McMoRan jumped almost 8%. — Scott Schnipper 5 Hours Ago IP shares fall after its board approves spinoff In this photo illustration, the International Paper logo seen on a smartphone and on a computer screen. Pavlo Gonchar | SOPA Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Shares of International Paper fell 4% after the packaging solutions company announced Monday that its board had approved the spinoff of its Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) packaging business into a publicly traded company, DS Smith. International Paper will remain an important shareholder, retaining a 19.9% stake. The company expects to complete the separation and distribution on Dec. 7, 2026, after the satisfaction of customary conditions and regulatory approvals are met. Additionally, the company announced its intention to delist from the London Stock Exchange after the completion of the separation. — Deena Zaidi 5 Hours Ago Artificial intelligence names are soaring as Huang returns to Nvidia A slate of stocks linked to the artificial intelligence trade skyrocketed on Monday as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. Dell Technologies and neocloud CoreWeave were last up about 22%, while data center power play Bloom Energy surged 19%. Photonics stock Lumentum popped 18%. Memory stocks also surged, with the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) gaining 19%. Rallies in SK Hynix and Micron Technology , both up around 20%, lifted the ETF. — Darla Mercado 6 Hours Ago Boeing shares rise after President Trump says he expects China to buy 250 more aircraft President of China Xi Jinping (L) shakes hands with U.S. President Donald Trump during an arrival ceremony at the White House on September 24, 2026 in Washington, DC. Chip Somodevilla | Getty Images News | Getty Images Shares of Boeing popped over 4% after President Donald Trump said on CNBC's " Squawk on the Street " that he expects China to buy another 250 Boeing jets. BA News of the additional aircraft orders comes roughly six months after the May summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Trump. At the time, Trump said that China would purchase 200 Boeing jets , an agreement that Beijing confirmed . — Ananya Chetia 8 Hours Ago CoreWeave, Oracle surge on Nvidia

headlines.article_text: Tech stocks see monster rally after Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Tech stock fortunes turned around following a torrid week for sector names that culminated in a steep sell-off Friday. Most major tech and AI buildout stocks rebounded. Nvidia bounced back sharply after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO. In this article NVDA CRWV NBIS GOOGL META MU Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 5:00 05:00 'Squawk on the Street’ crew react to Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO Squawk on the Street Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, sharply reversing Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020. Shares of Nvidia surged 31.48% after the company announced Monday morning that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO . The semiconductor giant gained back nearly $1 trillion in market cap, posting its best day since May 2003. Nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement followed a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month. The company has been embattled as reports surfaced about Huang's multiple extramarital affairs — one of which was with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang resigned as CEO of the company he founded on Nov. 12. The Nasdaq Composite surged 6.51% Monday, for its best day since April 9, 2025. The Nasdaq slid 10% last week, with tech stocks having a rocky week as investors remained nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models. All three major averages ended last week in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026. Nvidia stock chart Shares of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade saw a lift Monday on the Nvidia news. Shares of Alphabet surged 6.34%, Meta gained 6.55%, Amazon jumped 3.47% and Microsoft increased 1.65%. SpaceX added 4.35%, Arm Holdings surged 16.08% and AMD added 6.85%. Dell and Micron posted some of the sector's biggest gains of the day, gaining 20.46% and 19.04%, respectively. The iShares Semiconductor ETF gained 13.63%. Neoclouds, which have seen a particularly choppy few months amid AI boom financing concerns, surged on Huang's reinstatement. Nebius soared 20.28%, CoreWeave gained 22.32% and Iren gained 23.86%. Following a brief premarket surge, Anthropic shares posted a decline of 1.43% in its third day of trading. Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, before closing down 8.5% on Friday. "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was, he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about," Trump said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Trump said he spoke to Nvidia's board directly and that he "convinced" the board to reinstate Huang, who the president said "did nothing wrong." "That thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taking the whole market with it," Trump said, referring to Nvidia's stock price. headlines.title: Estimations initiales des ressources minérales sur les propriétés à redevances Wilson et Fenton de Cartier
headlines.summary: VAL-D'OR, Québec, 23 nov. 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ressources Cartier inc. (« Cartier » ou la « Société ») (TSXV : ECR; FSE : 6CA; OTCQB : ECRFF) est heureuse d'informer ses actionnaires des récentes nouvelles publiées par Epic Gold Corp. (CSE : EPG) (OTCQB : NFLDF) (FSE : 6341) (« Epic Gold ») au sujet de la propriété Wilson, située près de Lebel-sur-Quévillon, et de la propriété Fenton, située dans le district de Chapais-Chibougamau. Les deux propriétés se trouvent dans la ceinture de roches vertes de l'Abitibi, au Québec, Canada. La version originale et intégrale du communiqué d'Epic Gold est disponible sur SEDAR+ et sur le site Web d'Epic Gold.
